auditedScope: PCB Thermal Engineering & Spatial Thermal Conduction

findings.description: ThermodynamicsEngine only implements lumped 1D single-point equations (Fourier slab, Newton cooling, thermal stress). It lacks 2D/3D spatial temperature fields, discretized conduction operators, boundary conditions, and matrix assembly.
findings.remediation: Implement finite volume / conductance network spatial discretization on structured multilayer PCB meshes solving div(k grad T) + Q = 0.

findings.description: ThermalCaeEngine.solveThermalDistribution uses a 1D linear approximation deltaT = (Q * (L - x)) / (k*A + h*x*W) evaluated independently per node rather than solving a coupled matrix PDE [K]{T} = {Q}.
findings.remediation: Strengthen engineeringCore with a true discrete spatial thermal solver supporting anisotropic layer stackups and coupled boundary convection.

findings.description: The FEM thermal engine provides 2D/3D continuum element integration but is decoupled from canonical PCB stackup models (copper weight, dielectric layers, trace coverage, thermal vias, and component package thermal resistances R_theta_JC / R_theta_CS).
findings.remediation: Provide native PCB layer stackup modeling with in-plane (kx, ky) and through-plane (kz) effective anisotropic conductivity and package junction-to-case-to-board calculation.

findings.description: ThermalSolverBridge currently relies on 1D Fourier conduction and lumped resistance networks for verification rather than spatial multi-node PCB heat spreading benchmarks.
findings.remediation: Bridge spatial PCB thermal solver into SECP validation suite with exact energy conservation checks and canonical hashing.
